diagnosis: An algorithm for subclassification of VIN and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC)
legend: VIN or invasive SCC can be subclassified into three molecular subtypes (HPV-associated or HPV-independent, with the latter subclassified as p53abn or p53wt) using p16 and p53 immunostaining, with HPV nucleic acid testing, e.g. mRNA in situ hybridization, in cases where there are indeterminate results with immunostaining or if there is block-like positivity for p16 and mutant-type p53 expression. If NPV nucleic acid testing is not available, just p16 and p53 immunohistochemistry can be used; a large majority of VIN/carcinoma with block-like p16 and mutant-type p53 expression will be HPV-I. If neither immunohistochemistry nor HPV molecular testing is available, vulvar SCC and VIN can be diagnosed based on H&E morphology alone, e.g. SCC, HPV status undetermined.
